subject: math
title: Grade 2 Benchmarks of 25, 50 and 100: Closest Number, Halfway and Estimating
seo_title: Grade 2 Benchmarks of 25, 50 and 100 Worksheets: Free Math with Answer Key (BC Curriculum)
standard_text: Benchmarks of 25, 50, and 100 and personal referents
meta_desc: Free Grade 2 math worksheets on benchmarks of 25, 50 and 100 for the BC curriculum: find the closest benchmark on a number line, estimate jars and trays of beans, learn that halfway to 100 is 50, count by 25s with quarters and use personal referents in word problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: 25, 50 and 100 are friendly numbers. Find the one that is closest: 48 is closest to 50.
key_sub: Halfway to 100 is 50. Count by 25s: 25, 50, 75, 100. A handful of beans is about 25, so 4 handfuls are about 100.
body_html:
What is a benchmark?

A benchmark is a friendly number you know well. In Grade 2, the benchmarks are 25, 50 and 100 (and 0). We use them to think about other numbers. Is a number close to 25, 50 or 100?

Closest benchmark

Is 29 closest to 0, 25, 50 or 100?

29 is between 25 and 50. It is 4 away from 25 and 21 away from 50.

Answer: 25

Halfway and quarters

Halfway from 0 to 100 is 50, because 50 + 50 = 100. Count by 25s to cut 100 into 4 equal parts: 25, 50, 75, 100. A quarter coin is 25¢, and 4 quarters make 100¢, or $1.

Count by 25sQuartersPart of 100
251 quarter = 25¢a quarter
502 quarters = 50¢half
753 quarters = 75¢three quarters
1004 quarters = 100¢ = $1all of it

Estimate with a personal referent

A personal referent is something you know that is about 25, 50 or 100. A handful of beans is about 25. A Grade 2 class is about 25 students. Use it to estimate without counting.

Handfuls

A handful of beans is about 25. About how many beans are in 4 handfuls?

Count by 25s: 25, 50, 75, 100.

Answer: about 100

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
48 is closer to 25, because 4 is less than 548 is 2 away from 50 and 23 away from 25: it is closer to 50
10 is close to 100, because it looks the same10 is 90 away from 100. Look at the value
Counting 25, 50, 75, 80Keep adding 25: 25, 50, 75, 100
Halfway between 50 and 100 is 25Start at 50 and add half of the gap: 50 + 25 = 75
2 handfuls of 25 are about 27Count by 25s: 25, 50. About 50

faq.q: What are benchmarks of 25, 50 and 100 in Grade 2 math in BC?
faq.a: In the Number area of the BC Grade 2 math curriculum, students use 25, 50 and 100 as friendly numbers. They decide which benchmark a number is closest to and use benchmarks to estimate how many things are in a group.

faq.q: What is a personal referent in math?
faq.a: A personal referent is something familiar that shows about how many or how much, such as a handful of beans being about 25 or a class being about 25 students. Children use it to make good estimates without counting.
48 is closer to 50. It is only 2 away from 50 but 23 away from 25. Many children say 25 because they look only at the 4 in the tens place.

faq.q: How can I practise benchmarks of 25, 50 and 100 at home?
faq.a: Grab a handful of beans or pasta and count it, then ask: about how many are in 2 or 4 handfuls? Count by 25s with quarters, and ask whether numbers like 47 or 92 are closer to 25, 50 or 100.

items.q: Is 4 closest to 0, 25, 50 or 100?
items.e: 4 is between 0 and 25. It is 4 away from 0 and 21 away from 25. 0 is closer, so 4 is closest to 0.

items.q: Is 48 closest to 0, 25, 50 or 100?
items.e: 48 is between 25 and 50. It is 23 away from 25 and 2 away from 50. 50 is closer, so 48 is closest to 50. Do not look only at the tens digit: 4 tens is close to 5 tens.

items.q: Which number is closest to 50?
items.e: Count how far each number is from 50: 53 is 3 away, 60 is 10 away, 35 is 15 away, 5 is 45 away. The closest is 53. 35 has the same digits as 53, but it is much farther away.

items.q: Which number is closest to 100?
items.e: Count how far each number is from 100: 94 is 6 away, 80 is 20 away, 50 is 50 away, 10 is 90 away. The closest is 94. 10 looks like 100, but it is 90 away.

items.q: Which number is closest to 25?
items.e: Count how far each number is from 25: 27 is 2 away, 15 is 10 away, 40 is 15 away, 52 is 27 away. The closest is 27. 52 has the same digits as 25, but it is far away.

items.q: Which number is closest to 0?
items.e: Count how far each number is from 0: 3 is 3 away, 13 is 13 away, 20 is 20 away, 30 is 30 away. The closest is 3. 30 has a 3 in it, but it is 30 away from 0.

items.q: Which number is closest to 50?
items.e: Count how far each number is from 50: 46 is 4 away, 60 is 10 away, 64 is 14 away, 30 is 20 away. The closest is 46.

items.q: A full jar holds 100 marbles. About how many marbles are in this jar?
items.e: A full jar is 100. This jar is about half full. There are 48, so about 50 is the best estimate.

items.q: A full jar holds 100 marbles. About how many marbles are in this jar?
items.e: A full jar is 100. This jar is about a quarter full. There are 26, so about 25 is the best estimate.
The jar is almost full, and a full jar is 100. There are 97, so about 100 is the best estimate.

items.q: What number is halfway between 0 and 100?
items.e: There are 10 jumps of 10 from 0 to 100. Halfway is 5 jumps: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50. Answer: 50.

items.q: How many squares are coloured?
items.e: 5 rows of 10 are coloured: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50. That is 50, half of the 100 chart.

items.q: What is half of 100?
items.e: 50 + 50 = 100, so half of 100 is 50. 25 is a quarter of 100.

items.q: How many 50s make 100?
items.e: 50 + 50 = 100. That is 2 fifties.

items.q: Is the dot more or less than halfway to 100?
items.e: Halfway from 0 to 100 is 50. 62 is more than 50, so the dot is more than halfway.

items.q: Is the dot more or less than halfway to 100?
items.e: Halfway from 0 to 100 is 50. 38 is less than 50, so the dot is less than halfway.

items.q: Is the dot more or less than halfway to 100?
items.e: Halfway from 0 to 100 is 50. The dot is on 50, so it is exactly halfway.

items.q: Is the dot more or less than halfway to 100?
items.e: Halfway from 0 to 100 is 50. 90 is more than 50, so the dot is more than halfway.

items.q: What number is halfway between 0 and 50?
items.e: From 0 to 50 there are 10 jumps of 5. Halfway is 5 jumps: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25. Answer: 25.

items.q: A metre stick is 100 cm long. The arrow is halfway. What number is there?
items.e: Half of 100 cm is 50 cm. 50 cm + 50 cm = 100 cm.

items.q: How far is it from 50 to 100?
items.e: Count on by 10s from 50: 60, 70, 80, 90, 100. That is 5 tens, or 50. 150 adds 50 and 100.

items.q: Which number is more than halfway to 100?
items.e: Halfway is 50. Only 58 is more than 50. 50 is exactly halfway, not more.

items.q: Which number is less than halfway to 100?
items.e: Halfway is 50. Only 47 is less than 50. Look at the tens first: 4 tens is less than 5 tens.

items.q: A loonie is worth 100¢. How much is half of a loonie?
items.e: Half of 100¢ is 50¢. 50¢ + 50¢ = 100¢. 25¢ is only a quarter of a loonie.

items.q: What number is halfway between 50 and 100?
items.e: From 50 to 100 is 50. Half of 50 is 25. Start at 50 and add 25: 50 + 25 = 75. 25 is only the jump, not the number.

items.q: What number is halfway between 40 and 60?
items.e: 40 is 10 less than 50, and 60 is 10 more than 50. So 50 is halfway.

items.q: What number is halfway between 25 and 75?
items.e: 25 is 25 less than 50, and 75 is 25 more than 50. So 50 is halfway. 25 is only half of the gap.

items.q: 50 is halfway between 0 and what number?
items.e: From 0 to 50 is 50. Go 50 more: 50 + 50 = 100.

items.q: Ethan says halfway between 0 and 100 is 10. Is he right?
items.e: 10 is only 1 jump of 10. Halfway is 5 jumps of 10, which is 50. 50 + 50 = 100.

items.q: The path to the playground is 100 m long. Sofia stops halfway to tie her shoe. How far has she walked?
items.e: Halfway along 100 m is 50 m, because 50 + 50 = 100.

items.q: Count by 25s. What number comes next?
items.e: Count by 25s: 25, 50, 75, 100. 80 switches to counting by 5s.

items.q: Count by 25s. What is the missing number?
Count back by 25s. What number comes next?
items.e: Count back by 25s: 100, 75, 50, 25. 45 counts back by 5s.

items.q: What number is at the ? mark?
items.e: Halfway from 0 to 50 is 25. Each small jump is 5: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25.

items.q: What number is at the ? mark?
items.e: Halfway from 50 to 100 is 75. From 50, count 5 small jumps of 5: 55, 60, 65, 70, 75.

items.q: Which shows counting by 25s?
items.e: Add 25 each time: 25, 50, 75, 100. Answer: 25, 50, 75, 100. 25, 50, 70, 100 does not add the same number each time.

items.q: How many 25s make 100?
items.e: Count by 25s: 25, 50, 75, 100. That is 4 twenty-fives.

items.q: How many 25s make 50?
items.e: 25 + 25 = 50. That is 2 twenty-fives.
5 + 5 = 10 ones, which is 1 ten. 2 tens + 2 tens + 1 ten = 5 tens. Answer: 50. 40 forgets the new ten.
50 + 20 = 70, then 70 + 5 = 75. 70 forgets the 5 ones.

items.q: How many squares are coloured?
items.e: 2 full rows of 10 and 5 more: 10, 20, 21, 22, 23, 24, 25. That is 25, a quarter of the chart.

items.q: How many squares are coloured?
items.e: 7 full rows of 10 and 5 more: 70 + 5 = 75. 25 squares are white, and 75 + 25 = 100.

items.q: Which number is one quarter of the way from 0 to 100?
items.e: Cut 0 to 100 into 4 equal jumps: 25, 50, 75, 100. One quarter of the way is 25.

items.q: How much money is this?
items.e: A quarter is 25¢. Count by 25s: 25¢, 50¢. 10¢ counts them as nickels.

items.q: How much money is this?
items.e: Count by 25s: 25¢, 50¢, 75¢. 3¢ counts the coins, not the cents.

items.q: How much money is this?
items.e: Count by 25s: 25¢, 50¢, 75¢, 100¢. That is the same as $1.

items.q: 4 quarters have the same value as which coin?
items.e: 4 quarters are 100¢, and a loonie is $1 = 100¢. Answer: a loonie. A toonie is $2.
Count back by 25 from 100: 75. 75 + 25 = 100. 125 takes the smaller digit from the bigger one in each place.

items.q: Nadia has 75¢ in quarters. How many quarters does she have?
items.e: Count by 25s: 25¢, 50¢, 75¢. That is 3 quarters.

items.q: Wei has 3 quarters. How many more quarters does he need to make 100¢?
items.e: 3 quarters are 75¢. 75¢ + 25¢ = 100¢. He needs 1 more quarter.

items.q: A handful of beans is about 25 beans. Mei takes 2 handfuls. About how many beans does she have?
items.e: Count by 25s for each handful: 25, 50. So about 50. 27 adds 2 instead of 2 handfuls.

items.q: A handful of beans is about 25 beans. Owen takes 4 handfuls. About how many beans does he have?
items.e: Count by 25s: 25, 50, 75, 100. So about 100.

items.q: Ms. Lee’s Grade 2 class has 24 students. Is 24 closest to 0, 25, 50 or 100?
items.e: 24 is between 0 and 25. It is 24 away from 0 and 1 away from 25. 25 is closer, so 24 is closest to 25.

items.q: At the Terry Fox Run, Lucas’s class runs 46 laps of the field in all. Is 46 closest to 0, 25, 50 or 100?
items.e: 46 is between 25 and 50. It is 21 away from 25 and 4 away from 50. 50 is closer, so 46 is closest to 50.

items.q: On a field trip to a creek, Kai’s class counts 93 salmon. Is 93 closest to 0, 25, 50 or 100?
items.e: 93 is between 50 and 100. It is 43 away from 50 and 7 away from 100. 100 is closer, so 93 is closest to 100.

items.q: Zara sees 27 bald eagles in the trees by the river. Is 27 closest to 0, 25, 50 or 100?
items.e: 27 is between 25 and 50. It is 2 away from 25 and 23 away from 50. 25 is closer, so 27 is closest to 25.

items.q: A BC Ferries car deck has 100 spaces. 49 cars are on it. How full is the deck?
items.e: 49 is close to 50, and the deck holds 100. So it is about half full.

items.q: A BC Ferries car deck has 100 spaces. 26 cars are on it. How full is the deck?
items.e: 26 is close to 25, and the deck holds 100. So it is about a quarter full.

items.q: A BC Ferries car deck has 100 spaces. 97 cars are on it. How full is the deck?
items.e: 97 is close to 100, and the deck holds 100. So it is almost full.

items.q: Liam has 100 stickers. He gives half of them to his sister. How many does he keep?
items.e: Half of 100 is 50, because 50 + 50 = 100. 25 is a quarter, not a half.

items.q: A ribbon is 100 cm long. Ava cuts it in half. How long is each piece?
items.e: Half of 100 cm is 50 cm. 50 cm + 50 cm = 100 cm.

items.q: Nadia has 2 quarters. A loonie is 100¢. How much more does she need to make a loonie?
items.e: 2 quarters are 50¢. 50¢ + 50¢ = 100¢. She needs 50¢ more. 98¢ takes away 2 coins, not 50¢.

items.q: Ryan has 75¢. How much more does he need to make 100¢?
items.e: Count on from 75: 75 + 25 = 100. He needs 25¢. 175¢ adds instead.

items.q: A Grade 2 class has about 25 students. About 100 students come to an assembly. About how many classes is that?
items.e: Count by 25s: 25, 50, 75, 100. That is 4 classes.

items.q: Which is about 100?
items.e: One class is about 25 students. 4 classes: 25, 50, 75, 100. So the students in 4 classes is about 100. 2 hands have only 10 fingers.

items.q: Which is about 25?
items.e: A Grade 2 class has about 25 students, so the students in 1 class is about 25. 1 hand has 5 fingers and a week has 7 days.

items.q: Jasleen says 48 is closer to 25, because 4 is less than 5. Is she right?
items.e: 48 is 2 away from 50 and 23 away from 25. So 48 is closer to 50. Look at how far away it is, not only at the tens digit.

items.q: Arjun estimates there are 100 marbles in a jar. He counts 52. Was his estimate close?
items.e: 52 is 2 away from 50 and 48 away from 100. So 52 is closer to 50, and 100 was not close.

items.q: A Grade 2 class plants 50 cedar seedlings. A Grade 3 class plants 50 more. How many seedlings do they plant in all?
items.e: 50 + 50 = 100. 5 tens and 5 tens make 10 tens, which is 100.

items.q: Emma’s class wants to read 100 books in March. They have read 52 books. How far along are they?
items.e: 52 is close to 50, and 50 is halfway to 100. So they are about halfway.
